compliance.acoustic: 38.7 dB typical and 46.1 dB maximum with one supply, 39.3 and 48.2 with two (Table 4)

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation up to 1524 m (5,000 ft)
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 45 C (32 to 113 F), 40 C with 10GBASE-T transceivers (environmental requirements)

features.macsec: the SFP+ uplink ports are MACsec-enabled
features.optics-sfp-plus: the four uplink ports are 1GE or 10GE SFP+ ports (Table 8). With a 10GBASE-T transceiver the maximum ambient is 40 C
features.optics-sfp28: the four Virtual Chassis ports are 10GE or 25GE SFP28 ports (Table 8). VC formation is not supported with a 10GBASE-T transceiver in them
features.uplink-ports: four SFP+ ports take 1 GbE or 10 GbE transceivers, with MACsec
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 EX4100 switches. The four SFP28 ports are dedicated Virtual Chassis ports

management.console: RJ-45 console on the rear panel and RS232 to USB Type-C console on the front, both labelled CON
management.oob: management Ethernet RJ-45 on the rear panel, with a link activity lamp and a status lamp
management.usb: one USB 2.0 Type-A port on the rear panel

physical.depth-with-modules: 382.4 mm (15.05 in., 38.24 cm) with the power supply and fan modules installed (Tables 12 and 19)
physical.weight: 5.51 kg (12.15 lb) with the power supply and fan modules, 6495 g in Table 12 (Table 19)
physical.width-with-brackets: 482 mm (19 in.) with the mounting brackets attached (rack requirements)

power.poe-budget-w: 740 W with one supply, 1440 W with two (Table 32)
power.poe-standard: PoE+ on all 48 ports, 30 W per port by default (Table 12)
power.power-input-ac: 100 through 127 VAC or 200 through 240 VAC, 50 or 60 Hz (Table 30)

thermal.airflow: front to back, both fan modules and the supply marked AIR OUT (Table 27)

configs.description: The switch as shipped: one 920 W AC supply in slot 0, a cover panel over slot 1 and two front-to-back fan modules, all marked AIR OUT. A second supply raises the PoE budget from 740 W to 1440 W.
configs.name: ac

gaps.wanted: The HPE PSNow datasheet for the EX4100 line (a00150781enw) did not answer when fetched. It would carry the maximum power consumption and the thermal output that the hardware guide does not state.
A straight-on photograph of the EX4100-48P. Juniper's image-library paths returned a 404. The faces are drawn from the guide's renders (Figures 1 and 2), which are the only straight-on views held.

A per-port vocabulary for the Status lamp. Table 25 gives it meanings that depend on the mode the Factory Reset/Mode button chose (speed, duplex, administrative status, PoE), so the jack keeps the component's default off, link and activity states, and the mode lamps carry the meaning.
The size of the CLEI code label, the serial number label and the claim code label (Figure 13 callouts 2, 5 and 8). They are drawn as regions and not as parts.

The Junos interface names (ge-0/0/n, xe-0/1/n and xe-0/2/n). This guide names only the PIC numbers in Table 64, 0 for the RJ-45 ports, 1 for the SFP28 Virtual Chassis ports and 2 for the SFP+ uplink ports.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.
The diameter and depth of the Reset pinhole (callout 9). The guide names the Reset button and gives no size, so the hole is drawn at 2.0 mm as an estimate.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 4 bays (rear 4); `physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: Table 12 and Table 19 - height 1.72 in (4.37 cm), depth 13.78 in (35 cm) with no power supply and fan module and 15.05 in (38.24 cm) with them installed, width 17.36 in (44.09 cm) with the power supply and fan module installed and for all models (Table 19 note). 38.24 cm against 15.05 in (382.3 mm) differ by 0.1 mm and the cm figure is carried. The depth carried is the 350.0 mm of the bare chassis, and the modules add the rest, as for the EX3400. The body of 440.9 mm is the metal between the bracket fold lines. Weight is 6495 g with the supply and fan modules (Table 12) and 12.15 lb (5.51 kg) in Table 19; the two differ by 1.0 kg and Table 19 is carried because it is the table of chassis weights.

color.note: estimated - median of the bare face between the logo and the first jack block in Figure 10, #9397a0, and of the status panel, #434c59. Sampled from the guide's render, which may not match the metal.

drawing-vs-photo.note: No photograph of the real device is held. The guide's renders (Figures 10 and 11) are used for what is printed and where, and the line drawings (Figures 12 and 13) for the callouts. The renders print the port numbers in a salmon red on this PoE model (#ff8074, the median of the most saturated pixels) and in light grey on the non-PoE models; the line drawings print them black. The render wins.

ears.note: Figure 50 shows the two-post front-mounting brackets that ship (EX-RMK, Table 5, supplied) fitted flush with the front, and the guide's mounting topics give a 2 in. recessed position with the 2 in. recessed front-mounting brackets of the four-post rack-mounting kit EX-4PST-RMK (Table 5, orderable). The recess is 2 in. (50.8 mm). The wall-mount kit EX-WMK (Table 5, orderable) is a third mount. The kits are not listed under kits in this slice: the guide's parts are named but not modelled as kind kit contracts, and the figures place the brackets without a measurable fold line, so only the recess has an at.

earthing.note: Table 59 and Figure 71 - a two-hole protective earthing terminal on the rear panel, with two M5 by 10 mm screws with washers, orderable separately, and a Panduit LCD8-14A-L lug or equivalent. The holes are 16.9 mm apart on the render (the lug pitch is not stated in the guide). The two tapped holes are drawn as decor and the separately ordered screws are not drawn.

fru-bays.note: Table 11 and Table 53 - the switch ships with two fan modules and one 920 W AC supply, preinstalled. The supplies are fully redundant, load sharing and hot-removable and hot-insertable when the second supply is installed and running. The fan modules are hot-removable and hot-insertable and one is removed at a time. Do not mix AC and DC supplies, or supplies and fans of different airflow. Both supplies and fans are bays here; nothing in the chassis is built in. Transceivers are the third kind of FRU the guide names.

port-lamps.note: Figures 29 to 31 and Table 24 - each RJ-45 jack has a Link Activity lamp at one corner and a Status lamp at the other; the common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 housing carries both. Each SFP28 and SFP+ port has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp, drawn as arrows in the band between the two cage rows. Figure 30 numbers them 1, 1, 2, 2 across a column: down arrow, up arrow, down arrow, up arrow, so the down arrows belong to the lower port and the up arrows to the upper one. The pitch of the arrows within a column is read off the EX4100-24P render, whose right-hand block is the same. The Status lamp's colour shows speed (Table 25), so its states are not expressible as one vocabulary here (see gaps).

port-numbering.note: Figures 10 and 12 print 0 and 1, 2 and 3, up to 46 and 47 under the column pairs, with an up triangle after the even number and a down triangle before the odd one, so the upper jack of a column is the even port. The cages are printed 0 to 3 under each block the same way, and the uplink block is bracketed and labelled UPLINK. Table 64 names the PIC numbers - 0 for the RJ-45 ports, 1 for the SFP28 ports and 2 for the SFP+ uplink ports - and the interface names (ge-0/0/n and so on) are not printed on the metal and are not stated, so none is recorded.

ports.note: estimated - Figure 12 callout 2 and Figure 10 give 48 RJ-45 ports in three blocks of two rows and eight columns. Cavity edges were found along a pixel row of Figure 10: the columns are 41.3 px, 13.96 mm, apart, which is the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch, and the blocks start 117.5 mm apart (a 5.7 mm gutter after eight columns). The two rows are 14.31 mm apart (cavity centres 15.8 and 30.1 mm down) with the upper row turned 180 so that its lamp tabs face up, as rendered. The four SFP28 cages at 359.7 mm and the four SFP+ cages at 391.0 mm abut on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch, in two stacked rows on the jack rows' centres, the lower row turned 180 so that both lips face the band between them.

power.note: Table 32 - the EX4100-48P offers a 106 W system budget and 740 W of PoE with one 920 W supply (846 W in all), and 1440 W of PoE with two (1546 W in all of 1840 W). The guide gives no maximum power consumption for the switch, and its datasheet did not answer, so none is stated and the module power warning stands.

rear.note: estimated - Figure 11 and Figure 13. From the left, a lighter plate holds the MGMT RJ-45 over a USB 2.0 Type-A port in one housing, the CON RJ-45 and a claim code label area. Then come fan 0 and fan 1, each with a fan icon, its number and a round status lamp to its left, a plate with the earthing terminal (two holes on a lighter strip, with the earth symbol), the ESD point and two label areas (the CLEI code and the serial number), and power supply slots 0 and 1, each with a power icon and its number to its left. Measured at 2.957 px/mm from the 441.0 mm body. The 48-port models carry the claim code label on the rear (Figure 13 callout 2), where the 24-port models have it on the front.

rear-modules.note: estimated - the fan faces measure 124 by 125 px, 41.9 by 42.3 mm, 49.4 mm apart (82.3 and 131.7 mm from the left). The power supply faces measure 72.4 by 40.1 mm, 83.1 mm apart. The guide's module sizes (Table 20 note) are used for the bays (73.0 by 40.0 for a supply, 41.9 by 41.8 for a fan), centred on the measured faces. The second supply slot holds a cover panel, which the guide says to keep in an empty slot (the replacement procedures); the render shows two supplies fitted and Figure 13 shows the slot empty, so the default carries one.

scale.note: estimated - Gate 1 passed on Figure 14 (g022751), the 1500 px wide render of the EX4100-48T front, which has the same panel as the EX4100-48P of Figure 10 (g022750) and was the one measured. The body is 1310 px across (70 to 1379.5) and 129 px high, against 440.9 by 43.7 mm: aspects 10.15 and 10.09. So the figure is orthographic and is read at 2.97 px/mm. Figure 10 was checked against it by eye. The rear render, Figure 11 (g022752), reads about 2.957 px/mm.

sources.note: EX4100 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks (HPE), PDF created 2026-10-01, 281 pages, fetched from juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4100/ex4100.pdf: Tables 11 and 12 (the EX4100-48P model and specifications), Table 19 (chassis), Table 20 (module sizes and weights), Tables 26 and 27 (fan modules and airflow), Tables 29 to 34 (AC supplies and the PoE budget), Figures 10 to 13 (the front and rear of the EX4100-48P), Figures 29 to 32 (the lamps) and Figures 50 to 61 (mounting). The guide is copyright Juniper Networks and Hewlett Packard Enterprise; no terms of use are printed in it. Nothing of it is copied here, since every face is drawn new from measurements. The HPE PSNow datasheet (a00150781enw) did not answer (an HTTP/2 stream error on the one try), so no datasheet figure is used and the guide is the only maker source for the numbers. Juniper's image-library paths (ex4100-48p-front-high.jpg and the rear and the same for the 24P, 24T and 48T) all returned a 404 page, so no studio photograph is held. The community NetBox elevation of the EX4100-48P front and rear was fetched and used only to cross-check the three blocks of eight columns; no dimension is taken from it. End of life was searched on 2026-10-22 and no Juniper notice for the EX4100 was found, so the lifecycle is recorded as none announced.

status-block.note: estimated - Figure 10 and Figure 27. The four chassis lamps SYS, ALM, MST and CLD are in the left column of the dark panel at the right and the four port mode lamps SPD, DX, EN and PoE in the right column, each lamp above its legend, at 4.6 mm pitch. The Factory Reset/Mode button is a light-blue disc below them with a list symbol to its right (Figure 32), and the RS232 to USB Type-C console port, labelled CON, is below the button. Table 22 and Table 25 give the lamp meanings. The reset pinhole (callout 9 of Figure 12) is the dot printed between ports 44 and 45.
